name: Perindopril
summary: A long-acting ACE inhibitor prodrug with strong 24-hour blood-pressure control and EUROPA-trial evidence of cardiovascular-event reduction in stable coronary disease.
mechanism: Prodrug hydrolyzed to perindoprilat, which inhibits angiotensin-converting enzyme, lowering angiotensin II and increasing bradykinin.

pharmacokinetics.metabolism: Hepatic ester hydrolysis to active perindoprilat

dosing.adult: 4 mg once daily initially, titrated to 8 mg once daily

safety.pregnancy: Contraindicated in second and third trimesters (fetotoxic)
warnings: Dose-related rise in creatinine in renal impairment

clinicalPearls: EUROPA: perindopril 8 mg daily reduced cardiovascular death, MI, and cardiac arrest by ~20% in stable coronary disease.
Its long-acting perindoprilat half-life suits the popular perindopril/amlodipine fixed-dose combination for smooth 24-h control.
good: Hypertension with coexisting stable coronary disease; elderly patients.
bad: Angioedema history, pregnancy, or renal impairment without dose adjustment.

provenance.notes: Curated from standard pharmacology references (Goodman & Gilman, Katzung, Lexicomp-level standard facts). Values omitted where not confidently known — nothing invented.
